subject: Privatenet canary upgrade stall — rollback coordination & evidence request
messages:
From: Novamed Ops <ops@novamed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ingrid Sorensen <ingrid.sorensen@novamed.com>
Date: 2025-09-13 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private agent canary 1.6.2 — controlplane disconnects & 5xx spike

Hi Priya,

We started the canary roll of the privatenet agent 1.6.2 across 3 nodes in our eu-west-1 cluster this evening (around 21:30 UTC). Within ~8 minutes we saw transient controlplane reconnects and a spike of 5xx responses for inference traffic routed through the canary nodes. Traffic routed to non-canary nodes was unaffected.

We rolled the canary back manually at 21:45 but we retained logs and tcp traces for the affected nodes. Attaching a small archive of tcp traces and an uptime snapshot. Can you confirm receipt and whether Redwood has seen similar with 1.6.2 in other customers? We'd like an initial postmortem and any mitigation steps — this is a production-critical workflow.

Attachments: privnet-trace-09-13.tar.gz (logs/traces), uptime-snapshot-20250913.log

Thanks,
Ingrid
Senior SRE, Novamed Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Novamed Ops <ops@novamed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-13 22:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private agent canary 1.6.2 — controlplane disconnects & 5xx spike

Hi Ingrid — thanks for the quick report and the traces. We've received the attachment and have a triage team standing by.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus will validate the traces and reproduce the controlplane handshake behavior in our staging harness.
- We'll schedule an emergency bridge if we need packet-level debugging (do you have a preferred window within the next 3 hours?).
- We'll produce an initial summary and mitigation recommendations within 4 hours.

Can you also confirm whether you observed any management-plane API rate limiting on the Novamed side or any firewall logs that might show dropped management connections? That will help narrow whether this is an agent regression or a network interaction.

We're treating this as high priority.

— Priya
Principal Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Novamed Ops <ops@novamed.com>
Date: 2025-09-13 23:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private agent canary 1.6.2 — controlplane disconnects & 5xx spike

On Sat, Sep 13, 2025 at 22:40 Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Immediate plan: Marcus will validate the traces and reproduce the controlplane handshake behavior in our staging harness.

I've loaded the tcp captures and can reproduce repeated TLS handshake timeouts between the agent and the controlplane when the agent receives a specific management revision payload. The symptom reproduces with our private-test harness when we apply the same config blob Novamed provided (canary metadata attached). The handshake attempts back off and then the agent falls over into intermittent reconnects — that behavior lines up with the 5xx surge you saw.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: regression in the v1.6.2 control-channel state machine when receiving a sequence of rapid config deltas; the agent enters a bad retry state and exhausts ephemeral resources, causing request failures.

Action items I'll own now:
- Produce minimal reproducer and timeline (ETA 90m).
- Prepare a safe rollback patch and a config gating check we can run before re-rolling.
- Collect additional debug artifacts (agent heap/profile, kernel tcp stats) — attaching canary-deploy-metadata.json for reference.

If Novamed is open to a short bridge (we can do 00:30 UTC), we can walk through the tcp capture and discuss forcing a controlled rollback.

— Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ingrid Sorensen <ingrid.sorensen@novamed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-14 00:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private agent canary 1.6.2 — controlplane disconnects & 5xx spike

Thanks Marcus — 00:30 UTC works for us. We'll keep the traces available and can forward sysfirewall logs if you want them. No rate limiting observed on our side (we checked the API gateway) — we did see a brief bump in SYN retransmits concurrently with the failover, which we saved in the tcp dump.

Please go ahead with the rollback patch plan and the gating check you mentioned. We prefer to avoid re-rolling 1.6.2 until the root cause is validated.

— Ingrid
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Novamed Ops <ops@novamed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-14 08:55:00 +0000
Subject: Privatenet canary — rollback executed & initial impact summary

Team,

Quick update after the bridge and rollback: we coordinated a controlled rollback of the canary nodes at 01:05 UTC (Novamed time) using the safe rollback procedure. The rollback completed by 01:12 UTC and we validated service stability by sending synthetic inference requests for 20 minutes. Error rate returned to baseline.

What we collected and shared:
- Agent traces and heap profiles (privnet-trace-09-13.tar.gz) — see Drive link in related_links.
- Canary metadata we tested against (canary-deploy-metadata.json).
- Kernel tcp metrics and SYN retransmit samples (uptime-snapshot-20250913.log).

Next steps we committed to Novamed:
- Deep postmortem describing the sequence and definitive root cause (ETA 72 hours).
- A gating test for config delta sequences added to our pre-release pipeline.
- Offer of 2 days service credit for the impact window (subject to Novamed approval).

Novamed — can you confirm acceptance of the credit offer and whether you'd like the postmortem to be a written doc only or include a 30-minute walkthrough session with our engineering leads?

— Priya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ingrid Sorensen <ingrid.sorensen@novamed.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Privatenet canary incident — postmortem draft & evidence links

Hi Ingrid and team,

Attached is our draft postmortem and the evidence bundle:
- Root cause: configuration-delta handling regression introduced in agent 1.6.2 (state machine mismatch in control-channel).
- Impact window: 2025-09-13T21:38:00Z -> 2025-09-13T21:47:00Z (nodes under canary).
- Mitigation performed: immediate rollback at 21:45 UTC; synthetic validation and extended observation.
- Remediation: ships planned v1.6.3 with the state-machine fix and an additional gating test for rapid delta sequences.
- Compensation: Redwood proposals 2 service days credit to Novamed account; finance will follow up.

Evidence bundle (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-example-traces
Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4821

If Novamed would like a live walkthrough, we can schedule it early next week — please propose a couple of windows.

— Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
